rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21: An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases
rules.requirement: A proposed statewide ballot initiative would have capped annual rent increases for most residential rental units at the lesser of CPI or 5%, with exemptions for small owner-occupied buildings, new construction, certain subsidized units, short-term rentals, and nonprofit/religious facilities. The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court ruled the petition unconstitutional and blocked it from the November 2026 ballot because its religious-facility exemption violated Article 48's bar on initiatives relating to religion.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental units statewide, subject to listed exemptions
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units; newly constructed units less than 10 years old; certain publicly regulated units; short-term rentals; dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes
rules.citation: Mass. Initiative Petition 25-21 (2026); Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%. The petition included several exemptions, including owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is in a facility operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes, or is a publicly regulated/short-term rental unit

rules.conflict_note: This petition was blocked by the SJC from appearing on the November 2026 ballot and never took effect; it would have repealed the existing statewide ban on rent control (G.L. c. 40P) had it passed.

no_rule_findings.finding: Massachusetts currently maintains a statutory ban on rent control under G.L. c. 40P, which the blocked ballot initiative would have repealed; because the initiative failed, the existing statewide ban on local rent control remains in effect.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The petition would have repealed the Commonwealth’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P, and replaced it with a statewide cap on annual rent increases for most residential rental units.
